# Spotify Desktop Error Reference - Full Reference

Source: https://0iy.github.io/spotify-error-ref/
Repository: https://github.com/0iy/spotify-error-ref
Scope: Windows and macOS desktop client. 62 error codes documented.
Most client errors are shared across Windows and macOS; the installer codes differ per OS. Each entry below is tagged with the platform it applies to.
Unofficial community reference based on observed client behavior and user-reported reproduction cases. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotify AB.


## Authentication & Login

### auth:1 - Service temporarily unavailable
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Service is temporarily unavailable, please try again later."
Cause chain: App start -> Auth servers (AP cluster) -> TCP connect (port 443) -> Timeout
Causes:
  - Authentication servers down or overloaded
  - Network connectivity loss at startup
  - Firewall blocking outbound traffic to the AP cluster
Resolution:
  1. Check Spotify status at downdetector.com
  2. Restart device and router
  3. Log out and back in
  4. Add Spotify to Windows Firewall exceptions: Control Panel → Allow an app

### auth:2 - Authentication failure
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Service is temporarily unavailable, please try again later. - or - The username or password is incorrect."
Cause chain: Login form -> Auth request -> Token validation (server-side) -> Rejected
Causes:
  - Wrong username or password
  - Unstable connection causing auth timeout
  - Spotify server maintenance or outage
  - Expired cached session token
Resolution:
  1. Verify credentials - check Caps Lock
  2. Reset password at spotify.com/password-reset
  3. Check Spotify status page for outages
  4. Disable VPN temporarily
  5. Update the app: Help → About Spotify

### auth:3 - Firewall or proxy blocking auth
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify. Please update your firewall to allow Spotify."
Cause chain: Auth request -> Firewall -> Proxy / VPN -> AP server unreachable
Causes:
  - Windows Firewall rule blocking Spotify outbound
  - VPN routing through a blocked endpoint
  - Antivirus HTTPS inspection intercepting connections
  - Spotify entries in the system hosts file
Resolution:
  1. Add Spotify to Windows Firewall exceptions: Control Panel → Firewall → Allow an app
  2. Spotify Settings → Advanced → Proxy → No Proxy
  3. Disable VPN to test
  4. Check C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts for spotify.com entries and remove them

### auth:73 - Region mismatch or auth blocked
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Error code auth:73 - region or firewall block variant."
Cause chain: Auth request -> GeoIP check -> Country mismatch -> Rejected
Causes:
  - VPN routing through a country that doesn't match your account country
  - Account country setting outdated after relocation
  - Firewall blocking port 443
Resolution:
  1. Disable VPN before launching Spotify
  2. Update account country: spotify.com → Profile → Edit Profile → Country
  3. Spotify Settings → Advanced → Proxy → No Proxy
  4. Add Spotify to firewall exceptions

### accounts:4 - No internet connection detected
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "No internet connection detected."
Cause chain: netprofm (Windows NLA service) -> INetworkListManager (COM) -> Chromium NCN -> navigator.onLine = false -> Error shown
Causes:
  - netprofm service stopped or its registry keys are corrupted
  - INetworkListManager::IsConnectedToInternet() returning false despite working internet
  - VPN client causing Windows to report the adapter as offline
  - Spotify Offline Mode enabled in settings
  - Physical disconnection (WiFi / ethernet actually down)
Resolution:
  1. Open Services (Win+R → services.msc) → find "Network List" and "Network Location Awareness" → set both to Automatic and Start
  2. Admin PowerShell: sc start netprofm then sc start nlasvc
  3. Run: ipconfig /flushdns
  4. Check Spotify Settings → Playback → confirm Offline Mode is off
  5. In ncpa.cpl → disable unused virtual network adapters which can confuse the NLA service
Note: Why Firefox works but Chrome and Spotify fail: This error fires entirely client-side - no network request is ever made before showing it. The embedded Chromium layer reads navigator.onLine from the Windows Network Location Awareness service (netprofm) via a COM interface. When that service is broken, Chromium reports offline and Spotify shows this error. Firefox probes independently using its own network stack and ignores the Windows NLA result - which is why Firefox streams fine on the same machine while Chrome and Spotify both fail.

### accounts:3 - Incorrect username or password
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "The username or password is incorrect."
Cause chain: Login form -> accounts service -> Code 3
Causes:
  - Wrong username - try email address instead of display name
  - Wrong password - check Caps Lock and keyboard layout
  - Password changed on another device recently
Resolution:
  1. Verify exact email and password
  2. Reset password at spotify.com/password-reset
  3. If using a social account (Facebook/Google), use the matching login button rather than a password

### accounts:53–55 - Proxy blocking Spotify (HTTP 401 / 403 / 407)
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your internet network is blocking Spotify. Contact your network administrator. (53 = proxy 401 · 54 = proxy 403 · 55 = proxy 407)"
Cause chain: Auth request -> Proxy server -> HTTP 40x
Causes:
  - Proxy requires credentials that Spotify doesn't have
  - Corporate NTLM proxy authentication
  - Network policy explicitly blocking spotify.com
Resolution:
  1. Spotify Settings → Advanced → Proxy → enter proxy credentials
  2. Contact your network administrator for credentials or to whitelist Spotify
  3. If direct internet is available: Settings → Proxy → No Proxy

### accounts:103 - Firewall blocking account validation
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify. (Error code: accounts:103)"
Cause chain: App launch -> Firewall -> accounts API unreachable
Causes:
  - Windows Firewall blocking Spotify outbound on port 443
  - Antivirus HTTPS inspection intercepting connections
Resolution:
  1. Allow Spotify through Windows Defender Firewall (both Public and Private profiles)
  2. Spotify Settings → Advanced → Proxy → No Proxy
  3. Disable antivirus temporarily to test, then add Spotify as a permanent exception

### accounts:127 - Session terminated by server
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your session has been terminated."
Cause chain: Active session -> Server terminates -> Code 127
Causes:
  - Password changed on another device - all sessions invalidated
  - User clicked "Sign out everywhere" in account settings
  - Suspicious activity detected by Spotify security
Resolution:
  1. Log in again with current credentials
  2. Check email for a Spotify security notification
  3. Review sessions at spotify.com/account → Security and privacy

### accounts:402 - Critical client update required
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your client is being updated."
Cause chain: Login attempt -> Version check -> Below minimum -> Code 402
Causes:
  - Client version below Spotify's minimum supported version
  - Critical security patch required by the server
Resolution:
  1. Wait 1–2 minutes - the auto-updater should apply the patch automatically
  2. If stalled: download the latest version from spotify.com/download
  3. Run the installer as Administrator
  4. Free up disk space if the drive is nearly full (~200 MB needed)

### accounts:403 - Account disabled
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Account disabled."
Cause chain: Login -> Account status -> Suspended
Causes:
  - Terms of Service violation
  - Copyright or DMCA action
  - Fraudulent account activity
Resolution:
  1. Contact Spotify Support at support.spotify.com
  2. Submit an appeal via the Spotify support contact form

### accounts:406 - Device not allowed for this account
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Use of this device is not enabled for your account."
Cause chain: Login -> Platform check -> Code 406
Causes:
  - Account restricted to mobile-only platforms
  - Partner or enterprise plan with platform restrictions
Resolution:
  1. Contact Spotify Support to request desktop access
  2. Check whether your plan restricts desktop usage

### accounts:407 - Incomplete account profile
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "User profile is not fully updated, please update your profile and log out and back in."
Cause chain: Login -> Profile check -> Missing fields
Causes:
  - Account missing required fields (date of birth, country)
  - GDPR-required data update pending
Resolution:
  1. Complete profile at spotify.com/account/profile
  2. Log out then back in after saving
  3. Try completing the profile in the mobile app first if the website is unresponsive

### accounts:408 - Country mismatch
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your country does not match the one set in your profile."
Cause chain: Login -> GeoIP check -> Country mismatch -> Code 408
Causes:
  - Relocated without updating Spotify profile country
  - VPN making you appear in a different country
  - Free account used outside its registered country
Resolution:
  1. Disable VPN before logging in
  2. Update country: spotify.com → Profile → Edit Profile → Country
  3. Log out and back in after updating
  4. Upgrade to Premium to reduce geo-restrictions

### accounts:409 - Premium users only
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "This app is restricted to Premium users only."
Cause chain: Login -> Subscription check -> Free account
Causes:
  - Premium subscription lapsed - payment failed
  - Free account on a Premium-restricted client build
Resolution:
  1. Check subscription at spotify.com/account/subscription
  2. Update your payment method if the subscription lapsed
  3. Log out and back in to refresh subscription status

### accounts:413 - Email already registered
Severity: info
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Email is already connected to another user."
Cause chain: Signup -> Email lookup -> Conflict
Causes:
  - Email address already registered to a different Spotify account
Resolution:
  1. Click "Log in" instead of "Sign up"
  2. Use "Forgot password" to recover the existing account

### accounts:417 - Facebook credentials revoked
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "(No message shown - locale string is absent, a known client bug.)"
Cause chain: Facebook OAuth -> FB token -> Code 417 (blank message)
Causes:
  - Facebook access token revoked
  - Facebook account unlinked from Spotify
Resolution:
  1. Log in with Spotify username and password instead of Facebook
  2. Re-link Facebook at spotify.com/account/apps
  3. Use "Forgot password" to set a standalone password if you have none
Note: Known bug: accounts:417 has no English locale entry in the Spotify translation files. The error message area renders blank when this code fires.

### accounts:critical-update-error - Automatic update failed
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Please download the latest version from the Spotify website."
Cause chain: Spotify updater -> CDN download -> Write to disk -> Fails
Causes:
  - Insufficient disk space (~200 MB required)
  - Antivirus blocking SpotifyUpdate.exe
  - Permissions preventing write to %LocalAppData%\Spotify
  - Previous Spotify process locking files
Resolution:
  1. Download and install manually from spotify.com/download
  2. Run the installer as Administrator
  3. Ensure at least 500 MB free disk space
  4. End all Spotify processes in Task Manager before re-installing

### session:3 - Stored session token invalid
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "The username or password is incorrect."
Cause chain: App launch -> Token resume -> Token invalid
Causes:
  - Saved session token expired or invalidated
  - Password changed since last login
Resolution:
  1. Log out completely and log back in
  2. Delete cached prefs: close Spotify, delete %AppData%\Spotify\prefs , relaunch

### session:103 - Session handshake failed after browser login
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify. (Error code: session:103)"
Cause chain: Browser login -> spotify:// redirect -> Token exchange -> Fails
Causes:
  - Browser-to-app OAuth redirect blocked (spotify:// URI handler)
  - Corporate network intercepting HTTPS
  - Wrong default browser causing redirect failure
Resolution:
  1. Change default browser (Chrome ↔ Firefox) and try again
  2. Clear cache and cookies for spotify.com and accounts.spotify.com
  3. Change your Spotify password to use direct credential login, bypassing browser OAuth
  4. Sign out everywhere: spotify.com/account → Sign out everywhere
  5. Reinstall from Microsoft Store instead of the Spotify website, or vice versa

### desktop_login_accounts:2 - Browser login timed out
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Login timed out, please try again. - or - Signup timed out, please try again."
Cause chain: Browser opens -> User must act -> ~5 min timer expires -> Code 2
Causes:
  - User did not complete browser login in time
  - Browser tab closed before flow finished
  - Browser blocked the OAuth redirect back to Spotify
Resolution:
  1. Click "Log in" again and complete it promptly
  2. Ensure browser is not in Private/Incognito mode
  3. Ensure spotify.com redirects are allowed in your browser
  4. Try changing the default browser in Windows Settings
Note: Implementation detail: This is the only Spotify error code where the displayed message overrides the standard error dispatcher - it substitutes a dedicated timeout string based on whether the user was logging in or signing up.

### desktop_login_accounts:4 - OAuth token expired before use
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your session has expired, please try again."
Cause chain: Browser login -> Token generated (short TTL) -> Clock skew / delay -> Token expired
Causes:
  - Token TTL expired due to slow network delivering it to the app
  - System clock skew causing premature expiry
  - User delayed switching back to Spotify after browser finished
Resolution:
  1. Log in again and switch to Spotify immediately after the browser finishes
  2. Sync system clock: Win+R → w32tm /resync (run as Administrator)
  3. Settings → Time & Language → Date/Time → confirm "Set time automatically" is on

### desktop_login_accounts:5 - Firewall blocking OAuth callback
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify."
Cause chain: oauth2/v2/auth in browser -> redirect to desktop/auth/success -> callback blocked
Causes:
  - Windows Firewall blocking the Spotify.exe OAuth redirect
  - Corporate firewall blocking the spotify:// custom protocol
  - Third-party desktop widget app (Wallpaper Engine, Rainmeter) interfering with URI handler
Resolution:
  1. Click the "proxy settings" link in the error and check the proxy configuration
  2. Allow Spotify.exe in Windows Firewall - inbound and outbound
  3. Try a different network to confirm if this is network-specific
  4. Temporarily close Wallpaper Engine, Rainmeter, or similar apps
  5. Change your Spotify password to use credential login instead of OAuth
Note: The desktop OAuth round-trip. Browser login opens accounts.spotify.com/oauth2/v2/auth in your default browser; on success the browser is redirected to open.spotify.com/desktop/auth/success (failure goes to /desktop/auth/error), which hands the result back to the desktop app. If that final callback can't reach the app - firewall, a hijacked spotify:// URI handler, or the wrong default browser - the token never arrives.browser → https://accounts.spotify.com/oauth2/v2/auth?...
        → (user authorizes)
        → https://open.spotify.com/desktop/auth/success   // handed back to app
// callback blocked / hijacked → desktop_login_accounts:5

### accesspoint:17 - Access point rejected - region or firewall
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify. (Error code: 17 / accesspoint:17)"
Cause chain: Spotify app -> VPN / proxy -> AP cluster -> GeoIP rejection
Causes:
  - VPN routing through a foreign IP the AP cluster rejects
  - Account country doesn't match actual connection country
  - Firewall blocking AP ports (4070, 443)
Resolution:
  1. Disable VPN - Spotify Settings → Advanced → Proxy → No Proxy
  2. Update account country: spotify.com → Profile → Edit Profile → Country
  3. Restart Spotify after updating country
  4. Add Spotify to Windows Firewall exceptions
Note: What "accesspoint" means: This subsystem refers to Spotify's AP cluster - the persistent authenticated TCP connection the desktop app maintains for real-time features (playback sync, Spotify Connect). It is separate from the login and streaming servers.

### accesspoint:22 - Client version rejected by access point
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "This app is restricted to Premium users only. (Error code: accesspoint:22)"
Cause chain: Old client version -> AP handshake -> Version rejected
Causes:
  - Client too old - AP servers reject pre-2021 versions
  - Corrupted session state
  - Accumulated corrupted cache files
Resolution:
  1. Update Spotify: Help → About Spotify → Update now (resolves this in most cases)
  2. Download fresh installer from spotify.com/download or Microsoft Store
  3. Log out and back in
  4. Clear cache: Settings → Storage → Clear Cache
Note: Misleading message: Despite saying "Premium users only", this fires for all account tiers when the client version is too old. Spotify clients older than approximately April 2021 are rejected by AP servers.

## Network & Access

### accesspoint:31 - No internet - AP connection failed
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "No internet connection detected. (Error code: accesspoint:31)"
Cause chain: GET apresolve.spotify.com -> Resolve AP host -> Connect ap.spotify.com:4070 -> Fails
Causes:
  - Actual internet connectivity loss
  - Mobile data APN misconfiguration when using a hotspot
  - Network blocking the Spotify AP cluster
Resolution:
  1. Disconnect and reconnect - wait at least 60 seconds
  2. Verify internet works in a browser
  3. Try a different network (mobile hotspot) to narrow down the cause
Note: How the AP connection is actually made. Before opening its persistent socket, the client GETs apresolve.spotify.com to obtain the address of an access point in the nearest cluster, then opens an authenticated connection to that host (the ap.spotify.com family, port 4070/443). accesspoint:31 means that two-step connect never completed - DNS for apresolve failed, or the returned AP host was unreachable.GET https://apresolve.spotify.com/
// → { "ap_list": ["ap-gae2.spotify.com:4070", ...] }
connect(ap_list[0]);   // persistent authenticated socket
// either step fails → accesspoint:31

### accesspoint:39 - Hosts file or firewall blocking AP
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify. (Error code: accesspoint:39)"
Cause chain: apresolve / AP connect -> Hosts file / firewall -> Connection denied
Causes:
  - Hosts file contains entries blocking Spotify AP domains
  - Multiple network interfaces confusing IP routing
Resolution:
  1. Check C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts - remove lines containing "spotify"
  2. Win+R → ncpa.cpl → disable inactive or virtual ethernet adapters
  3. Run Spotify in Safe Mode with Networking to test whether a startup app is interfering
Note: The same two-step AP connect as accesspoint:31, blocked on this machine. Either the apresolve.spotify.com lookup or the follow-up AP socket is being refused locally - typically a hosts-file entry pointing a Spotify domain (apresolve, ap, or spclient) at a dead address, or a local firewall rule. Multiple active adapters can also send the AP connection out the wrong interface.

### accesspoint:50 - Network blocking Spotify at ISP or corporate level
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Your internet network is blocking Spotify. Contact your network administrator."
Cause chain: apresolve / AP connect -> ISP / corporate gateway -> Blocked upstream
Causes:
  - ISP, corporate, or school network blocking Spotify AP servers at network level
Resolution:
  1. Contact your network administrator to whitelist *.spotify.com and apresolve.spotify.com
  2. Use a mobile hotspot as a workaround
  3. A VPN can bypass network-level blocking in this specific case
Note: The same AP path, blocked upstream. Unlike accesspoint:39, the apresolve/AP connection isn't refused on your machine but by the network itself - an ISP, school, or corporate gateway dropping traffic to the Spotify AP cluster. Whitelisting *.spotify.com and apresolve.spotify.com at the gateway, or switching networks, restores it.

### EME_LICENSE_REQUEST_FAILED_WITH_STATUS - DRM license request returned HTTP error
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "License request failed (HTTP status code)."
Cause chain: CDM ready -> POST license challenge -> HTTP 4xx / 5xx
Causes:
  - License server temporarily down
  - Invalid or expired auth token
  - Network blocking HTTPS to Spotify license servers
Resolution:
  1. Retry playback after a few seconds
  2. Log out and back in to refresh the auth token
  3. Check HTTPS to *.spotify.com is not blocked
Note: Where it sits. After the CDM is available, the player still has to fetch a license: it POSTs a challenge to the license server and calls update() on the media-key session with the response. A non-2xx status raises EME_LICENSE_REQUEST_FAILED_WITH_STATUS; an empty body raises EME_LICENSE_REQUEST_EMPTY_RESPONSE. These are low-level ek faults with no message of their own, so they get wrapped into the default playback snackbar.resp = POST(licenseServer, keySession.challenge);
if (resp.status &gt;= 400) throw EME_LICENSE_REQUEST_FAILED_WITH_STATUS;
if (resp.body.empty)   throw EME_LICENSE_REQUEST_EMPTY_RESPONSE;
keySession.update(resp.body);   // → EME_LICENSE_UPDATE_FAILED on error
// any of these → ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE → default message

### Error 30 - Proxy or firewall blocking connections
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "A firewall may be blocking Spotify."
Cause chain: Network request -> System proxy -> Proxy / VPN
Causes:
  - Proxy configured in Windows system settings
  - VPN routing Spotify traffic incorrectly
  - Hosts file containing Spotify-blocking proxy redirect entries
Resolution:
  1. Spotify: Settings → Advanced → Proxy → No Proxy
  2. Windows: Settings → Network & Internet → Proxy → turn off "Use a proxy server"
  3. Disable VPN or configure split-tunnel to exclude Spotify
  4. Check C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts - remove Spotify-related entries

### com.spotify.installer −1 - Download failed (macOS installer)
Severity: error
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "An error occurred while trying to download Spotify."
Cause chain: Install Spotify.app -> HTTPS download -> Retry backoff -> Retries exhausted
Causes:
  - Spotify download server returned an HTTP error (4xx or 5xx)
  - No network connectivity, DNS failure, or TLS error
  - Request timed out
  - App Transport Security blocked a non-HTTPS redirect
Resolution:
  1. Check your internet connection and try again
  2. Disable any VPN or proxy and retry
  3. Temporarily disable antivirus HTTPS inspection / network filtering
  4. Download Spotify directly from spotify.com/download and open the .dmg yourself
Note: Exact flow. The download runs through an NSURLConnection delegate. Two checks can fail it: an HTTP response status of 400 or higher (the connection is cancelled), or a transport-level connection:didFailWithError: (DNS, TLS, or timeout). Either one enters a retry loop with a fixed backoff table - only once the retries are exhausted does the installer raise an NSError with code -1, which the dispatcher maps to the string key sInstallerOsxDownloadFailedErrorDescription.// connection:didReceiveResponse:
if (http.statusCode &gt;= 400) {
    [connection cancel];
    downloadFinishedWithError(httpError);    // -&gt; retry or fail
}

// downloadFinishedWithError: (retry guard)
if (downloadRetries &lt; maxRetryCount) {
    downloadRetries++;
    scheduleRetry(retryTable[downloadRetries]);   // backoff
} else {
    completeInstallWithError(                      // gives up -&gt; alert
        [NSError errorWithDomain:@"com.spotify.installer" code:-1 ...]);
}During the countdown the status label reads "Download failed. Retrying in %ds." The alert's "Download from Spotify.com" button opens spotify.com/redirect/install-failed.

### authorization-status (No connection) - Lost connection to Spotify (reconnecting)
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Couldn't connect to Spotify."
Cause chain: Active session -> AP socket drops -> AUTHENTICATION/CONNECTION_ERROR -> 500ms retry poll
Causes:
  - Network change (Wi-Fi ↔ ethernet, VPN toggled)
  - Mac/PC sleep-wake tore down the socket
  - Spotify access-point maintenance or rolling restart
  - Firewall rule changed while the app was open
Resolution:
  1. Wait - the client retries automatically with a countdown ("Retrying in…")
  2. Click Retry in the top-bar "No connection" badge
  3. Toggle Wi-Fi off and on, or reconnect your network
  4. If it persists, fully quit and reopen Spotify
Note: Why it's a badge, not an error page. This is the post-login reconnection path, separate from the login flow. The native access-point client keeps a persistent socket open; when it drops, the bridge fires an AUTHENTICATION_ERROR/CONNECTION_ERROR and the authorization-status component renders the top-bar badge and drives a countdown timer that auto-retries.// authorization-status component
onEvent(AUTHENTICATION_ERROR | CONNECTION_ERROR) {
  badge   = "No connection";
  title   = "Couldn't connect to Spotify.";
  setInterval(500ms, () =&gt; {            // countdown poll
    if (--secondsLeft &lt;= 0) reconnect(); // auto-retry with backoff
    else show("Retrying in " + secondsLeft + "...");
  });
}Because it auto-retries, a brief flash is normal after sleep/wake or a network switch - it only needs action if it stays stuck.

### NOT_AVAILABLE_OFFLINE - Offline mode is blocking playback
Severity: info
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Please turn off offline mode and try again."
Cause chain: Play track -> Offline mode + not downloaded -> NOT_AVAILABLE_OFFLINE
Causes:
  - Spotify Offline Mode is enabled
  - The track isn't downloaded for offline use
Resolution:
  1. Turn off Offline Mode (Spotify menu → toggle off Offline Mode)
  2. Download the track or playlist for offline use while online
Note: Reason NOT_AVAILABLE_OFFLINE in the waterfall. It only fires when the track isn't already downloaded; a downloaded track plays fine in offline mode. Distinct from the connection-lost badge, which is about an actual dropped socket.

### FRAGMENT_REQUEST_FAILED_WITH_STATUS - Audio segment download failed
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Spotify can't play this right now. If you have the file on your computer you can import it."
Cause chain: Next segment needed -> Audio CDN GET -> 403 / 404 / 503 -> retry  or  fatal
Causes:
  - CDN returned an error: 403 (license expired), 404 (track removed / cache miss), or 503 (overloaded)
  - Network interruption mid-stream
Resolution:
  1. Skip and replay the track - retryable errors recover automatically
  2. Log out and back in to refresh your license token
  3. Check your connection if many tracks fail in a row
Note: Retryable vs fatal. Audio streams in segments; each one is an HTTP GET to the audio CDN. When a segment returns a non-2xx status the player's error handler classifies it: transient statuses are retried with backoff and you never see anything, while a fatal one is wrapped into ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE and shown.// segment fetch → handlePlaybackError()
status = GET(audioCDN, segment);
switch (status) {
  case 503: case 500:  retryWithBackoff();      break;  // overloaded → silent
  case 403:            refreshLicense(); retry();  break;  // license expired
  case 404:            fatal();                    break;  // track removed / cache miss
}
// fatal → Z9.ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE → default snackbarSo a single failing track that recovers on replay is almost always a 403/expired-license; many tracks failing at once points at the network.

### max_subscriptions_reached - Too many Spotify instances open (tab limit)
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "You've got too many tabs open. Close this one and continue listening."
Cause chain: New session subscribes -> Concurrent count check -> max_subscriptions_reached
Causes:
  - Too many Spotify tabs or instances open on the same account
Resolution:
  1. Close other Spotify tabs or windows
  2. Quit duplicate Spotify instances and reopen a single one
Note: A route-level error page, not a playback snackbar. Each open client/tab takes a "subscription" to the account's player state; opening one past the allowed concurrent count renders the max_subscriptions_reached error page on the newest one. Closing any other instance frees a slot immediately.

### offline device-limit-reached - Offline device limit reached
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Remove all downloads from another device to listen offline with this one."
Cause chain: Start offline download -> License server device count -> count ≥ limit
Causes:
  - Too many devices already have offline downloads for this account (typically 5)
Resolution:
  1. Remove downloads from a device you no longer use
  2. Spotify allows offline downloads on a limited number of devices per account
Note: Enforced server-side at download-authorization time. When you start a download the client asks the license server to authorize offline use; the server counts how many devices already hold offline content for the account and rejects the request past the cap (typically 5). It is about the download step, not playback - already-downloaded tracks keep working.

### connect.device-picker (restricted / unsupported) - Can't connect to this device
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Sorry, we can't connect to this device. / Update this device and the Spotify app."
Cause chain: Device picker -> Reachability / version / rights check -> Restricted / outdated / off-network
Causes:
  - Target device firmware too old ("No longer works with Spotify")
  - Devices on different Wi-Fi networks
  - Account restricted from this device type
Resolution:
  1. Put both devices on the same Wi-Fi network ("Check your WiFi")
  2. Update the target device firmware and the Spotify app
  3. Wake the device and retry
Note: One device-picker, several distinct states. The Spotify Connect picker maps each failure to its own string: firmware too old → "No longer works with Spotify"; devices on different networks → "Check your WiFi"; account not allowed on the device type → "Not available for your account"; asleep → "Connect to WiFi and wake device". They share the same picker UI, so the fix depends on which sub-message you actually see.

## DRM & Playback

### EME_NO_SUPPORTED_KEYSYSTEM - No DRM key system available
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Playback of protected content is not enabled."
Cause chain: Spotify JS -> EME API call -> Widevine CDM -> No CDM found
Causes:
  - Widevine CDM not installed or disabled in the browser/Chromium layer
  - DRM playback disabled in browser settings
  - Ad-blocker extension interfering with Widevine
  - Old browser without Web EME support
  - Linux: Widevine binary not present
Resolution:
  1. Chrome: go to chrome://components/ → Widevine Content Decryption Module → Check for update
  2. Chrome: go to chrome://settings/content/protectedContent → enable Play protected content
  3. Disable all browser extensions and retry
  4. For Spotify desktop app: reinstall it - the CEF Widevine bundle is included in the installer
  5. Linux: sudo apt install libwidevinecdm0 or enable Widevine in your browser settings
Note: Root cause of the "Firefox works, Chrome fails" pattern: Firefox probes network state independently and does not depend on Windows NLA. It also has its own DRM stack. Chrome (and Spotify's embedded Chromium layer) fully trust the Windows NetworkChangeNotifier for online state and require the system Widevine CDM for DRM. When either is broken, Chrome and Spotify fail together while Firefox continues normally.

### DISALLOW_PROTECTED_TRACK_ERROR - DRM disabled - protected content blocked
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Protected tracks not supported."
Cause chain: Play track (DRM protected) -> Platform DRM check -> DRM unavailable
Causes:
  - DRM disabled in browser settings
  - Enterprise browser policy disabling EME
Resolution:
  1. Chrome: Settings → Content → Protected Content → Allow
  2. Check chrome://policy/ for policies disabling EME
  3. Use the Spotify desktop app (independent DRM stack)
Note: Distinct from the "CDM missing" page. When a track is flagged DRM-protected but the platform reports no usable protection, the engine raises DISALLOW_PROTECTED_TRACK_ERROR - this is one of the few ek faults with its own dedicated text ("Protected tracks not supported.") rather than the generic message. If instead the key system itself is absent you get EME_NO_SUPPORTED_KEYSYSTEM and the full "Playback of protected content is not enabled" page.if (track.isProtected &amp;&amp; !platformDrmAvailable)
    throw DISALLOW_PROTECTED_TRACK_ERROR;   // "Protected tracks not supported."

### CAPPING_USER_IS_CAPPED - Free tier monthly listening limit reached
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "User is capped."
Cause chain: Play request (free tier) -> Monthly quota check -> USER_CAPPING_REACHED
Causes:
  - Free plan listening quota for the month exhausted
Resolution:
  1. Wait for the monthly limit to reset on the 1st
  2. Upgrade to Spotify Premium
Note: Opens an upsell, not a snackbar. In the dispatcher waterfall the USER_CAPPING_REACHED reason is handled before the default text - it opens the capping/Premium upsell modal instead of a one-line message. The underlying CAPPING_USER_IS_CAPPED engine fault is what flags the play request as over-quota.if (reasons.has(USER_CAPPING_REACHED))
    return openCappingUpsell();   // Premium prompt, before default snackbar

### MEDIA_DECODING_ERROR - Audio decoding error
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Media decoding error."
Cause chain: Audio segment (from CDN) -> Media element decode -> error.code === 3
Causes:
  - Corrupted audio segment from CDN
  - Codec unsupported by platform
  - Hardware decoder failure
  - Insufficient system resources
Resolution:
  1. Skip the track - if only one track fails, it is likely a corrupted CDN segment
  2. Restart Spotify to reset the audio pipeline
  3. Update graphics and audio drivers
  4. Try disabling hardware acceleration in Spotify Settings
Note: Surfaced by the media element. MEDIA_DECODING_ERROR is the engine's name for the browser media element firing error code 3 (MEDIA_ERR_DECODE) - the bytes arrived but the decoder rejected them. (Its siblings: code 2 → MEDIA_NETWORK_ERROR, code 4 → MEDIA_NOT_SUPPORTED.) It wraps into the default playback error.audioEl.onerror = (e) =&gt; {
  switch (audioEl.error.code) {
    case 2: throw MEDIA_NETWORK_ERROR;   // MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK
    case 3: throw MEDIA_DECODING_ERROR;  // MEDIA_ERR_DECODE  ← here
    case 4: throw MEDIA_NOT_SUPPORTED;   // MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED
  }
};A single bad track that plays fine on retry is usually a corrupt CDN segment; every track failing points at the local audio/graphics stack (drivers, hardware acceleration).

### Exclusive mode playback failure - Content won't play in exclusive audio mode
Severity: warn
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "Exclusive mode is on, so this content won't play. Turn it off in settings to keep listening."
Cause chain: Exclusive audio mode (CoreAudio) -> Unsupported content type
Causes:
  - Spotify is holding exclusive CoreAudio access to the output device
  - The content type being played isn't supported while exclusive mode is on
Resolution:
  1. Turn off exclusive mode: Spotify Settings → Playback → disable exclusive output
  2. Play the content, then re-enable exclusive mode afterwards if you want it
Note: macOS only. Exclusive mode takes exclusive CoreAudio access to the output device; some content types can't play while it is engaged.

### CLIENT_VERSION_SUNSETTED - Client version no longer supported
Severity: fatal
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "(Forced update modal - playback is blocked until you update.)"
Cause chain: Handshake / license resolve -> Version check -> Sunset → forced modal
Causes:
  - Spotify servers no longer support this client version
  - License API version too old for the current client
Resolution:
  1. Update Spotify to the latest version
  2. macOS: download the current installer from spotify.com/download
  3. Restart Spotify after updating
Note: A pre-switch special case. Unlike the playback-restriction reasons, a sunset version doesn't produce a snackbar - it short-circuits before the dispatcher switch and opens a blocking update modal. It can be signalled two ways: the access-point handshake/playback response flags the version, or the license resolver returns a deprecated-version code.if (event.code == CLIENT_VERSION_SUNSETTED ||
    ekError == LICENSE_RESOLVER_DEPRECATED_VERSION) {
    openForcedUpdateModal();   // playback blocked until updated
    return;                    // never reaches the snackbar switch
}

### ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE (playback dispatcher) - How playback errors become on-screen messages
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Spotify can't play this right now. If you have the file on your computer you can import it."
Cause chain: Track load fails -> ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE -> reasons[] waterfall -> snackbar / modal
Causes:
  - A track failed to load for any of the reasons handled in the waterfall (region, Premium, offline, capping, user-ban)
  - A low-level engine fault (DRM, fragment, decode) that has no specific reason, so it shows the default message
Resolution:
  1. Identify the specific reason from the message shown, then see the matching entry below
  2. Skip and replay - transient faults recover automatically
  3. Log out and back in to refresh tokens if many tracks fail
Note: One switch drives every playback snackbar. When a track can't play, the engine emits a ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE event carrying a reasons[] array. A single dispatcher walks those reasons in priority order and returns the first match - which is why a region block wins over a Premium gate, and that over offline mode. A few reasons skip the switch and open a modal instead. This is the shared layer behind most of the playback entries below, identical on macOS and Windows.switch (event.code) {
  case ONE_TRACK_UNPLAYABLE:
    if (reasons.has(AGE_ASSURANCE_REQUIRED))      return openAgeModal();        // pre-switch
    if (reasons.has(EXPLICIT_CONTENT_FILTERED))   return openExplicitModal();    // pre-switch
    if (reasons.has(NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_REGION)) return "...in your region...";
    if (reasons.has(NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_NON_PREMIUM))    return "Spotify can't play this right now.";
    if (reasons.has(NOT_AVAILABLE_OFFLINE))           return "turn off offline mode and try again";
    if (reasons.has(USER_CAPPING_REACHED))            return openCappingUpsell();
    if (reasons.has(BANNED_BY_USER_ARTIST))           return "allow this artist in the phone app";
    return "Spotify can't play this right now. ...import it.";   // default
  case TIMEOUT:
    return "Network connection failed while playing this content.";
}The low-level engine faults (DRM, fragment, decode) don't print their own text - they get wrapped into this event and fall through to the default message, unless they map to a more specific reason.

### NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_REGION - Track not available in your region
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Spotify can't play this track in your region. If you have the file on your computer you can import it."
Cause chain: Play track -> Server region check -> NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_REGION
Causes:
  - Track licensing doesn't cover your account's country
  - VPN making you appear in a different region
  - Account country is out of date
Resolution:
  1. Disable VPN and retry
  2. Update your account country at spotify.com → Edit Profile
  3. Import a local copy of the file if you own it
Note: Reason NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_REGION - the highest-priority non-modal branch of the playback dispatcher above, so it wins over a Premium gate or offline mode when several reasons apply at once. The region is decided server-side from your account country, not the track UI.

### NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_NON_PREMIUM - Track requires Premium
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Spotify can't play this right now."
Cause chain: Play track (free tier) -> Premium check -> NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_NON_PREMIUM
Causes:
  - Track or feature is Premium-only on a free account
Resolution:
  1. Upgrade to Spotify Premium
  2. Choose a track available on the free tier
Note: Reason NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_NON_PREMIUM in the dispatcher waterfall (just below region). The generic "can't play this right now" text is intentional - the same string is reused for several Premium-gated cases, which is why the message looks vague.

### BANNED_BY_USER_ARTIST / _TRACK - Artist or track hidden by you
Severity: info
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "We can't play this until you allow this artist in the Spotify phone app."
Cause chain: Play track -> Account block list -> BANNED_BY_USER_*
Causes:
  - You previously hid or blocked this artist or track
  - The block list is managed from the Spotify mobile app
Resolution:
  1. Open the Spotify phone app and allow the artist or track again
  2. On desktop, some accounts can unblock via "You asked us not to play this artist"
Note: Reasons BANNED_BY_USER_ARTIST / BANNED_BY_USER_TRACK in the waterfall. The block list is account-level (set from the mobile app), so the desktop client can't always clear it - hence the message points you back to the phone app. Some accounts also see the desktop variant "You asked us not to play this artist."

### AUDIO_FORMAT_NEGOTIATION_FAIL - Audio format negotiation failed
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "(Opens an audio format negotiation dialog.)"
Cause chain: Track load -> Propose formats -> Server accepts none
Causes:
  - Client and server couldn't agree on an audio codec / format to use
Resolution:
  1. Restart Spotify and retry
  2. Update to the latest version
  3. Change audio quality in Settings → Playback
Note: Also a pre-switch modal. On track load the client proposes a set of audio formats/codecs; if the server accepts none of them, the engine raises AUDIO_FORMAT_NEGOTIATION_FAIL, which bypasses the snackbar switch and opens a dedicated format dialog rather than a one-line message.formats = proposeAudioFormats();        // by quality + codec support
if (!server.accepts(formats))
    dispatch(AUDIO_FORMAT_NEGOTIATION_FAIL); // → open format dialog
Changing the audio-quality setting changes which formats are proposed, which is why toggling it often clears this.

### video-unsupported-key-system - Video DRM not available
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Hmm... we can't seem to play this content. Try installing the latest version of Spotify."
Cause chain: Play video -> requestMediaKeySystemAccess() -> No key system
Causes:
  - Video DRM (key system) not available in this client
  - Client too old for video playback
Resolution:
  1. Update to the latest Spotify version
  2. Restart Spotify after updating
  3. Reinstall if video still won't play
Note: EME probe failed for video. Protected video asks the embedded browser layer for a key system via requestMediaKeySystemAccess(); if none is available (or the API throws NotSupportedError), playback fails with this message. It is the video sibling of the audio "Playback of protected content is not enabled" / EME_NO_SUPPORTED_KEYSYSTEM path.try {
  await navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess(
        ["com.widevine.alpha", ...], cfg);   // CDM probe
} catch (NotSupportedError) {
  show("Hmm... we can't seem to play this content. " +
       "Try installing the latest version of Spotify.");
}

### fatal-error / error.generic - Something went wrong (client UI error)
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Something went wrong. / An error occurred. (RELOAD PAGE)"
Cause chain: UI render -> Unhandled JS throw -> non-fatal dialog  or  fatal page
Causes:
  - Unclassified client-side error in the app UI
  - Corrupted cache or a transient render fault
Resolution:
  1. Click "Reload page" if it is offered
  2. Restart Spotify
  3. Clear cache: Settings → Storage → Clear cache
  4. Reinstall if it keeps happening
Note: The genuine UI-layer fault. Unlike the playback errors, this isn't a dispatched event - it's the React UI itself throwing during render. A non-fatal throw shows the "Something went wrong / Try reloading the page" dialog; a fatal one replaces the view with an "An error occurred" page and a RELOAD PAGE button. A corrupt cache is the most common repeatable cause.

## Installer

### Installer error 18 - Files locked by another process
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "The installer is unable to install Spotify because the files to write to are in use by another process."
Cause chain: NSIS installer -> Write to disk (%AppData%\Spotify) -> Files locked -> Error 18
Causes:
  - Previous Spotify processes still running (SpotifyWebHelper, SpotifyUpdate)
  - Comodo Firewall or iTunes holding a lock on shared files
  - Steam background services locking files
Resolution:
  1. Open Task Manager - end all Spotify-related processes
  2. Close Steam completely
  3. Delete the folder %AppData%\Roaming\Spotify then retry
  4. Clean boot: Win+R → msconfig → Services → Hide Microsoft → Disable All → restart → install
  5. Try the Microsoft Store version as an alternative

### Installer error 24 - Incompatible install environment
Severity: error
Platform: Windows
Displayed message: "Spotify installation error code 24."
Cause chain: NSIS installer -> Environment check -> Conflict found
Causes:
  - Conflicting software running during installation
  - Malware preventing installer from writing files
  - Corrupted installer download
Resolution:
  1. Close all other applications before installing
  2. Run a malware scan
  3. Download a fresh installer from spotify.com/download (do not reuse a cached .exe)
  4. Try installing in Safe Mode with Networking

### com.spotify.installer −2 - Extraction failed (macOS installer)
Severity: error
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "An error occurred while trying to extract Spotify."
Cause chain: Mounted disk image -> Copy Spotify.app -> Copy fails
Causes:
  - Destination disk is full
  - Spotify.app missing from the mounted image (corrupt download)
  - Destination folder not writable
  - Disk image unmounted mid-copy
Resolution:
  1. Free up disk space, then retry
  2. If Spotify is already open, quit it first ("Please quit Spotify and try again") and retry
  3. Delete any partial Spotify.app in /Applications or ~/Applications, then reinstall
  4. Re-download a fresh .dmg from spotify.com/download
Note: What it actually is. "Extraction" here means copying Spotify.app off the mounted disk image to the install location. Before copying, the installer picks a destination - ~/Applications if writable, otherwise /Applications (which sets needsAuthorization = true). It also force-quits any running Spotify first; if Spotify won't quit within 5 seconds you get a separate "Please quit Spotify and try again" prompt instead of this error. Code -2 is raised only when the unprivileged copy itself fails.// moveBundleToApplicationsFolderFromMountPoint:
dst = writable(~/Applications) ? ~/Applications : /Applications

for (app in runningApplications)            // pre-flight
    if (app.bundleURL.path == dst) {
        [app terminate]; pollUntilTerminated(5s);
        if (!terminated) return showQuitSpotifyAlert();
    }

if (!CopyApplication(srcURL, dstURL, uid, gid))   // the copy
    error = [NSError ... code:-2];           // "extraction failed"So a code -2 almost always means the destination ran out of space, the app bundle was missing from a corrupt image, or the volume was unmounted mid-copy.

### com.spotify.installer −3 - Disk image mount failed (macOS installer)
Severity: error
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "An error occurred while trying to mount the downloaded Spotify disk image."
Cause chain: Downloaded .dmg -> hdiutil attach -> exit≠0  OR  no /Volumes/
Causes:
  - Corrupt or truncated .dmg download
  - macOS security (Gatekeeper) blocked mounting from a temporary location
  - A disk image with the same volume name is already mounted
  - No free loop device available to attach the image
Resolution:
  1. Eject any existing Spotify volume in Finder, then retry
  2. Re-download the installer - a truncated file is the most common cause
  3. Restart the Mac to clear stale mounts and retry
  4. Mount the .dmg manually by double-clicking it, then drag Spotify into Applications
Note: Two independent checks raise this. The installer mounts the downloaded image by shelling out to hdiutil, then inspects the result twice: the process must exit zero and its stdout must contain a /Volumes/ mount path. If either check fails, it raises code -3 with the same message.// installDMG:error:
NSTask: /usr/bin/hdiutil attach &lt;dmg&gt; -noautoopen -noidme -nobrowse

if (task.terminationStatus != 0)             // check 1: exit code
    return error(code:-3);

output = readStdout();
if ([output rangeOfString:@"/Volumes/"].location == NSNotFound)  // check 2
    return error(code:-3);

mountPoint = substringFrom("/Volumes/");      // successSo check 1 fires on a corrupt/truncated download or a Gatekeeper-blocked mount; check 2 fires in the rare case hdiutil succeeds but reports the volume somewhere other than stdout (e.g. a name collision with an already-mounted Spotify volume).

### com.spotify.installer −4 - Install failed (macOS installer)
Severity: error
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "An error occurred while trying to install Spotify."
Cause chain: Copy to Applications -> AuthorizationCopyRights -> Privileged copy fails
Causes:
  - Wrong admin password, or admin authorization denied
  - Destination (/Applications) not writable or protected by System Integrity Protection
  - Disk full during the privileged copy
  - Old Spotify.app locked or still in use
Resolution:
  1. Enter the correct administrator password when prompted
  2. Quit Spotify completely (including the menu-bar item) before installing
  3. Install to ~/Applications (your home folder) to avoid needing admin rights
  4. Free up disk space, then retry
Note: The privileged path. When the destination needs admin rights, the installer requests system.privilege.admin via AuthorizationCopyRights and then runs the copy as a sequence of privileged shell commands. Any failure in that chain returns false, which the caller turns into code -4.status = AuthorizationCopyRights(authRef,
            {"system.privilege.admin"},
            {"prompt":"Spotify needs permission to install."}, ...);

if (status == errAuthorizationCanceled)   // -60006: user hit Cancel
    { didUserCancel = YES; return NO; }   //   → silent abort, NO alert
if (status != errAuthorizationSuccess)    // wrong password / denied
    return NO;                            //   → code -4 → alert

// with rights, via AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges:
//   mv old aside · cp -pR src dst · chown · chmod · find -exec chmod · rm -rf old
// any step failing → return NO → code -4Cancelling is special: clicking Cancel on the password prompt is errAuthorizationCanceled (−60006) and aborts silently - the window just stays open, no "Installation Failed" alert. A wrong password, a SIP-protected destination, or a disk-full during the privileged cp all surface as code -4.

### com.spotify.installer (generic) - Generic install failure (macOS installer)
Severity: error
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "An error occurred while trying to install Spotify."
Cause chain: writeToFile: / OS error -> Unmapped code -> default branch
Causes:
  - A file-write error while saving the downloaded image to a temp folder (e.g. out of space)
  - An operating-system error not mapped to a specific installer code
Resolution:
  1. Free up disk space - the installer writes a temporary copy of the .dmg before installing
  2. Restart and retry
  3. Download and install manually from spotify.com/download
Note: The catch-all branch. Every fatal error funnels through one dispatcher that turns the NSError code into a message. It only special-cases -1, -2, -3, -4; anything else hits the default branch and shows the generic install-failed string.// friendlyDescriptionForErrorCode:
switch (code) {
  case -1: key = sInstallerOsxDownloadFailedErrorDescription;   break;
  case -2: key = sInstallerOsxExtractionFailedErrorDescription; break;
  case -3: key = sInstallerOsxMountFailedErrorDescription;      break;
  case -4: key = sInstallerOsxInstallFailedErrorDescription;    break;
  default: key = sInstallerOsxGenericErrorDescription;          // here
}The most common real cause that lands here is the temp-file write in the "write the downloaded image to disk" step: if writeToFile: fails (typically out of space), its raw Cocoa/POSIX NSError is passed straight through the dispatcher and falls into this default branch.

### Unsupported Platform (macOS) - macOS version too old for this installer
Severity: fatal
Platform: macOS
Displayed message: "Sorry, this version of Spotify is for macOS 12.0 or later."
Cause chain: applicationDidFinishLaunching -> Gestalt version check -> major < 12
Causes:
  - Mac is running macOS 11 (Big Sur) or earlier
  - The current Spotify installer requires macOS 12 (Monterey) or newer
Resolution:
  1. Click "Find installers for older versions" in the dialog to get a compatible build
  2. Update macOS to 12.0 or later if your Mac supports it
  3. Use an older Spotify installer compatible with your macOS version
Note: The check. Right after launch the installer calls isSupportedPlatform, which reads the OS major/minor version through the legacy Gestalt() API and compares it against _spMinSupportedOSVersion = "12.0". This is a separate alert path - it is not a com.spotify.installer error code, so it shows its own "Unsupported Platform" dialog rather than "Installation Failed".// isSupportedPlatform
Gestalt('sysv1', &major);   // OS major
Gestalt('sysv2', &minor);   // OS minor
return (major &gt;= 12);       // _spMinSupportedOSVersion = "12.0"

// applicationDidFinishLaunching:
if (!isSupportedPlatform)
    showUnsupportedPlatformAlert();   // → "Find installers for older versions" / terminateNote the Info.plist lists LSMinimumSystemVersion 10.11, but this runtime check is what actually enforces macOS 12.

## Web API

### HTTP 401 - invalid_client - Wrong app credentials
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "{"error": "invalid_client", "error_description": "Invalid client secret"}"
Cause chain: POST /api/token -> Basic auth check -> 401 invalid_client
Causes:
  - Wrong client_id or client_secret in your code
  - Using credentials from the wrong Dashboard app
  - Secret regenerated but old value still in use
Resolution:
  1. Verify credentials in developer.spotify.com/dashboard
  2. If the secret was regenerated, update it in your code or environment variables
Note: Fails at the token endpoint. The token request authenticates the app with HTTP Basic auth (base64(client_id:client_secret)); a mismatch returns 401 invalid_client before any scope or user check. A regenerated secret invalidates the old one immediately.POST https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token
Authorization: Basic base64(client_id + ":" + client_secret)
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials
// wrong id/secret → 401 {"error":"invalid_client"}

### HTTP 403 - PREMIUM_REQUIRED - Player control requires Premium
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Player command failed: Premium required"
Cause chain: PUT/POST /v1/me/player -> User-token + Premium check -> 403 PREMIUM_REQUIRED
Causes:
  - User does not have Spotify Premium
  - Using Client Credentials OAuth flow for player endpoints (user auth flow required)
Resolution:
  1. Ensure the user has Spotify Premium
  2. Use Authorization Code Flow or PKCE - not Client Credentials - for all /me/player/* endpoints
Note: Two preconditions, one error. The /v1/me/player/* endpoints require both a user-authorized token (Authorization Code or PKCE - never Client Credentials) and a Premium account. Missing either yields 403 PREMIUM_REQUIRED. A Client-Credentials token has no user attached, so it can never satisfy these endpoints.PUT /v1/me/player/play
Authorization: Bearer &lt;user-token, scope user-modify-playback-state&gt;
// free account OR app-only token → 403 {"reason":"PREMIUM_REQUIRED"}

### HTTP 404 - NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE - No active Spotify device
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Player command failed: No active device found"
Cause chain: Player command -> Active-device lookup -> 404 NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE
Causes:
  - No Spotify client open on user account
  - Stale cached device ID - it changes each session
  - Spotify left in fully idle state
Resolution:
  1. Ensure a Spotify client is open before making player API calls
  2. Call GET /v1/me/player/devices to refresh the list before issuing commands
  3. Pass an explicit device_id in the request body
Note: The API has no device to target. Player commands act on the account's active device. If no client is currently playing/idle-active, or the cached device_id has rotated (it changes per session), the command returns 404 NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE. Refresh the device list first, or pass an explicit device_id.GET  /v1/me/player/devices            // → list, pick an id
PUT  /v1/me/player/play?device_id=&lt;id&gt; // target it explicitly
// no open client / stale id → 404 NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE

### HTTP 403 - RESTRICTION_VIOLATED - Playback restriction violated
Severity: error
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "Player command failed: Restriction violated"
Cause chain: Player command -> actions.disallows check -> 403 RESTRICTION_VIOLATED
Causes:
  - Skipping in a context that disallows it (radio, free tier)
  - Attempting to control playback when not the active controller
Resolution:
  1. Check the disallows object in GET /v1/me/player before issuing the command
  2. Ensure Premium for full playback control API access
Note: The context said no. Every playback context exposes a disallows object listing actions that aren't currently permitted (e.g. skipping in radio, seeking in an ad). Issuing a disallowed action returns 403 RESTRICTION_VIOLATED. Check disallows before acting rather than catching the error.GET /v1/me/player
// → { "actions": { "disallows": { "skipping_next": true, ... } } }
if (!state.actions.disallows.skipping_next) skipNext();
// otherwise → 403 RESTRICTION_VIOLATED

### HTTP 429 - Too Many Requests - Rate limit exceeded
Severity: warn
Platform: Windows & macOS
Displayed message: "HTTP 429 Too Many Requests - see Retry-After header."
Cause chain: Burst of requests -> Rolling-window limiter -> 429 + Retry-After
Causes:
  - Sending too many requests per unit time
  - Polling-based architecture making rapid repeated calls
Resolution:
  1. Implement exponential backoff using the Retry-After value in the response header
  2. Cache API responses to reduce repeated identical requests
  3. Use Spotify Connect state events instead of polling /v1/me/player
Note: Honor the header, don't guess. Spotify rate-limits on a rolling window per app; when you exceed it the response is 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds). The correct handling is to wait exactly that long, then resume - fixed sleeps either waste time or get throttled again.resp = await fetch(api);
if (resp.status === 429) {
  const wait = Number(resp.headers.get("Retry-After")) * 1000;
  await sleep(wait);          // exact backoff from the server
  return retry();
}Polling /v1/me/player is the usual culprit; cache responses or use Connect state events instead.
